genZNote: Indole positive is the whole difference between this and P. mirabilis — both swarm across the plate like they own it.

morphology.motility: Highly motile (peritrichous flagella) — characteristic swarming motility on agar

habitat.naturalHabitat: Human and animal GI tract; widely distributed in soil, water, and decaying organic matter
habitat.hostAssociation: Normal gut flora in some individuals; opportunistic pathogen
habitat.environmentalOccurrence: Common in soil, sewage, and decomposing matter

culture.growthCharacteristics: Facultative anaerobe; characteristic concentric-ring 'swarming' growth pattern on non-inhibitory agar
culture.colonyMorphology: Non-lactose-fermenting colonies; swarms in a thin film across blood agar unless swarming is suppressed

identificationClues: Gram-negative rod with characteristic swarming motility across agar surfaces
Rapid urease positive — predisposes to struvite (staghorn) kidney stones by alkalinizing urine
Indole positive — distinguishes P. vulgaris from P. mirabilis (indole negative)
Phenylalanine deaminase positive, a genus-defining Proteus/Morganellaceae trait

diseases: Urinary tract infections, often associated with struvite/staghorn calculi
Occasional bacteremia in hospitalized or catheterized patients
virulenceFactors: Urease — hydrolyzes urea to ammonia, alkalinizing urine and promoting struvite stone formation
Swarming motility and fimbriae aiding colonization of the urinary tract
clinicalImportance.transmission: Endogenous gut flora; catheter-associated or healthcare-associated transmission
clinicalImportance.epidemiology: A recognized cause of complicated and catheter-associated UTIs, particularly linked to struvite stone formation via urease activity
clinicalImportance.labSignificance: Indole testing separates P. vulgaris from the more commonly encountered P. mirabilis; swarming can obscure other organisms on a mixed culture plate

examFacts.importantTest: Indole test (positive) distinguishes from P. mirabilis; rapid urease test
examFacts.distinguishingFeature: Swarming, urease-positive, indole-positive Gram-negative rod — indole positivity is the key differentiator from P. mirabilis
